scenario: [LREG.8.1] — non-greedy quantifiers are RE2 syntax, and POSIX does not REJECT them, it SILENTLY REINTERPRETS them. `a+?` is lazy one-or-more to RE2. POSIX ERE has no lazy repetition, so it reads the same characters as `(a+)?` — zero-or-one of a greedy plus — which can match the EMPTY STRING. Against "bbb" the two engines therefore disagree about whether the pattern matches at all: RE2 requires at least one `a` and does not match, POSIX matches empty at position 0 and does. The rule must NOT fire, so the expected count is 1 (the Log fact alone). This is the security-relevant direction of the divergence — a guard that should reject its input accepts it, with no error at any layer. Chosen over a match-shape test on purpose: DS compiles with REG_NOSUB and matching is boolean, so greedy-vs-lazy is unobservable unless it changes WHETHER a pattern matches.
rules_ds:
schema Log scope logical:
    msg: String key

schema Hit scope logical:
    d: Int key

rule r:
    Log e where e.msg ~ /a+?/
->
    emit Hit logical d: 0
